This article compares the 30-day mortality rates following acute surgery for patients with a Charlson Comorbidity Index score of 3 or higher across [[danmark|Danmark]], its five regions, and individual hospitals. This supplementary indicator (9c) tracks outcomes for a highly vulnerable patient population, making it a critical measure of acute surgical care quality and postoperative management.

Nationally, the current mortality rate stands at 17.9% (95% CI: 15.2-20.9) based on 133 deaths out of 742 patients [^src1]. At the regional level, [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] reports the lowest mortality rate at 13.1%, while [[nordjylland-region-i-alt|Nordjylland Region i alt]] reports the highest at 25.4% [^src1]. The remaining regions fall between these extremes: [[sjaelland-region-i-alt|Sjælland Region i alt]] at 16.2%, [[midtjylland-region-i-alt|Midtjylland Region i alt]] at 17.9%, and [[syddanmark-region-i-alt|Syddanmark Region i alt]] at 23.2% [^src1].

When examining individual hospitals, there is significant variation in outcomes, heavily influenced by patient volume and case mix. [[sygehus-soenderjylland|Sygehus Sønderjylland]] records the highest mortality rate among all facilities at 34.8% (8 deaths out of 23 patients) [^src1]. [[rigshospitalet|Rigshospitalet]] also shows a high rate of 30.0%, though this is based on a very small denominator of just 20 patients, resulting in a wide confidence interval (11.9-54.3) [^src1]. Conversely, [[amager-og-hvidovre-hospital|Amager og Hvidovre Hospital]] achieves the lowest reported mortality rate among hospitals with unsuppressed data, at 10.0% [^src1]. Two hospitals, [[bornholms-hospital|Bornholms Hospital]] and [[regionshospitalet-randers|Regionshospitalet Randers]], have their exact patient counts suppressed (marked as #/#) due to low volumes, yielding mortality rates of 0.0% and 4.5% respectively, but with extremely wide confidence intervals that preclude definitive statistical comparisons [^src1].

Historical data included in the table allows for trend analysis across the 2022/23, 2023/24, and current reporting periods. Nationally, the mortality rate increased slightly from 20.2% in 2022/23 to 21.2% in 2023/24, before dropping to the current 17.9% [^src1]. This recent national improvement is mirrored in several regions and hospitals. For example, [[hospitalerne-i-nordsjaelland|Hospitalerne i Nordsjælland]] saw a dramatic improvement, falling from a peak of 28.3% in 2022/23 to 15.4% in 2023/24, and further down to 13.0% currently [^src1]. Similarly, [[holbaek-sygehus|Holbæk Sygehus]] reduced its rate from a high of 36.0% in 2023/24 to 25.0% in the current period [^src1]. However, not all trends are positive; [[rigshospitalet|Rigshospitalet]] fluctuated significantly, dropping from 33.3% in 2022/23 to 18.8% in 2023/24, before rising again to 30.0% in the current period [^src1].
